title: Android SlidingDrawer: state events
purpose: Check that the host receives a notification when the SlidingDrawer finishes opening or closing.
changes: The drawer now queues completed Opened and Closed state changes for the host to drain. The example displays the latest event beneath the drawer.
steps: Tap the drawer handle to open it. After it finishes moving, the text Drawer opened should appear beneath it.
Tap the handle again to close it. After it finishes moving, the text should change to Drawer closed.
Turn on Lock handle, then use Open programmatically and Close programmatically. The event text should still update after each movement.
Choose OK if it works, or Reject with details and your device.
expected: Each completed state change is reported once, including programmatic changes while the handle is locked.
limits: This covers open and close state events, not Android's scroll start/end listeners. Exact Android timing and device parity remain unverified.
validation: Ten SlidingDrawer Rust tests and 157 XML importer tests passed, including event timing, deduplication, interruption and bounded retention.
A 320 × 760 browser test checked event text for touch and locked programmatic changes.
